title: SECURITY: Fix SQL injection risk in PRAGMA journal_mode interpolation
description:
CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: Journal mode PRAGMA in src/database.py (line 504) uses f-string interpolation: cursor.execute(f'PRAGMA journal_mode = {mode};') with mode from environment variable. Although validated against allowlist, PRAGMA statements don't support parameterized queries.

**Attack Vector:** If allowlist validation is bypassed or extended, arbitrary SQL could be injected via DB_JOURNAL_MODE env var.

**Impact:** Database schema manipulation, data exfiltration, potential RCE via SQLite extensions.

**Remediation:**
1. Keep strict allowlist validation
2. Consider using hardcoded PRAGMA statements for each allowed mode instead of interpolation
3. Add additional validation

**Files to modify:**
- src/database.py: Fix PRAGMA journal_mode interpolation

title: SECURITY: Fix CORS misconfiguration - wildcard origins with credentials
description:
CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: CORS middleware in src/app.py (line 476) configured with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True simultaneously, which is invalid per CORS spec and allows any origin to make authenticated requests.

**Attack Vector:** Malicious website can make authenticated requests to API endpoints using victim's browser session/cookies.

**Impact:** CSRF-like attacks, credential theft, unauthorized actions on behalf of authenticated users.

**Remediation:**
1. Either restrict allow_origins to specific trusted domains OR set allow_credentials=False
2. Never use wildcard with credentials
3. Configure via environment variable for production vs development

**Files to modify:**
- src/app.py: Fix CORS middleware configuration

title: SECURITY: Remove hardcoded default API key from frontend and backend
description:
CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: Hardcoded default API key 'ema-vwap-admin-2026' embedded in DEFAULT_SETTINGS constant in src/web/app.js (line 92) and used as fallback in src/app.py.

**Attack Vector:** Any attacker who discovers this default key can authenticate to all admin endpoints including database management, paper trading control, and settings modification.

**Impact:** Full administrative compromise - database wipe, settings manipulation, paper trading engine control, credential theft.

**Remediation:**
1. Remove hardcoded default from src/web/app.js DEFAULT_SETTINGS
2. Require explicit API_KEY environment variable in src/app.py
3. Fail closed if not configured (no default)
4. Rotate any exposed keys immediately

- src/auth/dependencies.py: Add proper validation

# Plumb Optuna Search Range Settings Through Batch Sweep

> **Bead**: `ema_vwap-lm6` — Plumb Optuna search range settings through batch sweep pipeline

## Problem

The **single-symbol optimizer** correctly reads all Optuna search range settings from `Settings → Optuna Search Ranges` and sends them to the backend. The **batch sweep** ignores all of them (except `min_trades`, just fixed) and always uses hardcoded code defaults. It also hardcodes `strategy_mode: "auto"` with no UI to change it.

## Full Gap: 14 Settings + 1 UI Control

| Setting | Default | Single Optimizer | Batch Sweep |
|---------|---------|------------------|-------------|
| `fast_ema_min/max` | 3 / 30 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `slow_ema_min/max` | 10 / 100 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `trend_ema_min/max` | 50 / 250 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `volume_multiplier_min/max` | 0.8 / 3.5 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `atr_multiplier_min/max` | 1.0 / 6.0 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `risk_reward_min/max` | 1.0 / 6.0 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `vwap_slope_max_bound` | 0.003 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `n_jobs` | 1 | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `n_startup_trials` | null | ✅ from settings | ❌ code default |
| `seed_base_params` | true | ✅ from settings | ❌ hardcoded `true` |
| `strategy_mode` | "auto" | ✅ from UI dropdown | ❌ hardcoded `"auto"` |

## Proposed Changes

### Layer 1: Frontend HTML — [index.html](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/web/index.html)

Add a **Strategy Mode** `<select>` dropdown to the batch sweep panel, matching the "Optuna Setup Scope" on the backtest page:

```html
<label>Strategy Mode</label>
<select id="batch-strategy-mode-select">
  <option value="auto">Auto (Compare All 3 Setups)</option>
  <option value="crossover">Setup 1: EMA × VWAP Crossover</option>
  <option value="multi_ema">Setup 2: Multi-EMA Confirmation</option>
  <option value="vwap_pullback">Setup 3: VWAP Pullback Entry</option>
</select>
```

---

### Layer 2: Frontend JS — [app.js](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/web/app.js#L2544-L2559) `startBatchSweep()`

Read all 14 settings from `getSettings()` and the new dropdown:

```js
const s = getSettings();
body: JSON.stringify({
  // ... existing fields ...
  strategy_mode: document.getElementById("batch-strategy-mode-select")?.value || "auto",
  min_trades: s.min_trades,           // already fixed
  fast_ema_min: s.fast_ema_min,
  fast_ema_max: s.fast_ema_max,
  slow_ema_min: s.slow_ema_min,
  slow_ema_max: s.slow_ema_max,
  trend_ema_min: s.trend_ema_min,
  trend_ema_max: s.trend_ema_max,
  volume_multiplier_min: s.volume_multiplier_min,
  volume_multiplier_max: s.volume_multiplier_max,
  atr_multiplier_min: s.atr_multiplier_min,
  atr_multiplier_max: s.atr_multiplier_max,
  risk_reward_min: s.risk_reward_min,
  risk_reward_max: s.risk_reward_max,
  vwap_slope_max_bound: s.vwap_slope_max_bound,
  n_jobs: s.n_jobs !== undefined ? s.n_jobs : 1,
  n_startup_trials: s.n_startup_trials,
  seed_base_params: s.seed_base_params !== false,
})
```

---

### Layer 3: API Model — [app.py](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/app.py#L684-L701) `BatchOptimizeRequest`

Add 14 optional fields with defaults matching `OptunaConfig`:

```python
class BatchOptimizeRequest(BaseModel):
    # ... existing fields ...
    # Search ranges (default to OptunaConfig defaults)
    fast_ema_min: int = 3
    fast_ema_max: int = 30
    slow_ema_min: int = 10
    slow_ema_max: int = 100
    trend_ema_min: int = 50
    trend_ema_max: int = 250
    volume_multiplier_min: float = 0.8
    volume_multiplier_max: float = 3.5
    atr_multiplier_min: float = 1.0
    atr_multiplier_max: float = 6.0
    risk_reward_min: float = 1.0
    risk_reward_max: float = 6.0
    vwap_slope_max_bound: float = 0.003
    n_jobs: int = 1
    n_startup_trials: Optional[int] = None
    seed_base_params: bool = True
```

Forward all to `BatchOptimizerConfig` in [`start_batch_optimize()`](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/app.py#L734-L759).

---

### Layer 4: Batch Optimizer — [batch_optimizer.py](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py)

**`BatchOptimizerConfig`** ([L51-69](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py#L51-L69)): Add 14 matching fields.

**`_run_single_optuna()`** ([L135-148](file:///c:/crypto/ema_vwap/src/batch_optimizer.py#L135-L148)): Forward all range fields to `OptunaConfig`:

title: Auto-scale WFO num_windows and trials_per_window from candle count and n_trials
description: Currently num_windows (default 5, UI-settable) and trials_per_window (hardcoded 15 in app.js, 20 in WFORequest default) are static. When users provide 180 days of 5m candles (~51,840 bars) with n_trials=1000, these values are severely under-scaled. Implement a compute_wfo_auto_params(n_bars, n_trials) helper in wfo.py that derives: (1) num_windows targeting 10-20 day OOS windows at 5m, scaled with bar count; (2) trials_per_window as floor(n_trials / num_windows) clamped to [25, 150] so TPE has enough startup trials per window. Wire into WalkForwardEngine when num_windows=0 (auto sentinel). Expose auto mode in WFORequest. Update app.js UI to show computed values. Backward-compatible with explicit values.

title: Implement Background Job Worker, Progress Polling & Centralized Settings Store
description:
Build foundational backend execution infrastructure:
1. Background Job Manager: Async task worker with SQLite/in-memory job status tracking for long-running historical data syncs, Optuna optimizations, and Monte Carlo runs with progress polling (/api/tasks/{id}).
2. Centralized Settings & Secrets Store: SettingsManager saving API keys, broker credentials, and system preferences to local .env or SQLite with masked UI retrieval.
3. Structured Logging: Configure rotating file logging (logs/app.log, logs/paper.log) with FastAPI log integration.
design: Add src/tasks.py for background job execution and status tracking. Create src/settings.py for local configuration storage. Configure logging in src/app.py.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Long-running syncs and optimizations run in background with real-time progress updates via API.
2. SettingsManager safely saves and retrieves API keys without exposing secrets in plaintext or committing to Git.
3. Structured logs are written to rotating file handlers in logs/ directory.

title: Implement Abstract Data Provider Adapter Architecture & Timezone Pipeline
description:
Refactor data ingestion in src/data_loader.py into a pluggable BaseDataProvider adapter architecture. Includes:
1. BaseDataProvider Abstract Interface: Standardized fetch_historical_candles(), get_supported_timeframes(), and normalize_symbol() contract.
2. Concrete Adapters: Extract GeminiAdapter, KuCoinAdapter, and SyntheticAdapter into src/providers/ package.
3. Timezone & Timestamp Normalization: Ensure all incoming timestamps are parsed and stored as standard ISO-8601 UTC with session timezone conversion helpers for US/Eastern stock markets.
4. Provider Registry: Dynamic provider discovery and routing based on exchange/asset_type.
design: Create src/providers/base.py, src/providers/crypto.py, and src/providers/synthetic.py. Refactor DataLoader in src/data_loader.py to dispatch to registered providers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Data ingestion uses BaseDataProvider subclass adapters with zero code duplication.
2. All candles are validated and saved in normalized UTC timestamps.
3. Existing Gemini, KuCoin, and Synthetic data loaders pass all unit tests.

title: Harden SQLite Database Engine with WAL Mode, Concurrency Tuning & Performance PRAGMAs
description:
Upgrade and harden the local database layer (src/database.py) to handle concurrent multi-asset reads and writes across background historical data syncs, paper trading ledger logging, and high-speed Optuna backtests.

Key Improvements:
1. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL Mode): Enable 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;' on connection initialization to allow non-blocking concurrent readers while writes are occurring.
2. High-Throughput PRAGMA Configuration: Set 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;', 'PRAGMA cache_size=-64000;' (64MB memory page cache), and 'PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY;' for fast bulk candle insertions and queries.
3. Concurrency & Busy Timeout Handling: Configure 'sqlite3.connect(..., timeout=30.0)' with a thread-safe connection manager to prevent 'database is locked' errors under concurrent workloads.
4. Optimized Compound Indexing: Verify and tune compound indexes across (exchange, symbol, timeframe, timestamp) for sub-millisecond range lookups.
5. Schema Support for Multi-Asset & Ledger Tables: Prepare database schema abstractions for candles, paper trading ledger, Optuna per-asset profiles, and portfolio balances.
design:
1. In src/database.py, enhance DatabaseManager with connection context manager configuring WAL mode, synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size, and timeout.
2. Add automated retry/backoff logic for write operations.
3. Create test suite in tests/test_database_concurrency.py to validate concurrent reads/writes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All SQLite connections initialize in WAL mode with 30s busy timeout and 64MB cache.
2. Concurrent background candle syncs run without throwing database locked errors while backtests are reading.
3. Bulk insert and range query benchmarks show noticeable performance improvement.
4. Regression tests pass with 100% stability under multi-threaded read/write load.

title: Implement Dynamic Price Precision for Sub-Penny & Micro-Cap Tokens (BONK, SHIB, PEPE)
description: Fix price rounding truncation where prices < 0.0001 (such as BONK at .000018) were rounded to 0.0 or clamped to 0.0001, causing distorted 100% win rates and artificial PnL. Implement dynamic precision up to 8-10 decimals.

(2) Convert candles table to hypertable: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb; CREATE TABLE candles (...); SELECT create_hypertable('candles', 'timestamp', chunk_time_interval => INTERVAL '1 day'); (3) Add compression policy: ALTER TABLE candles SET (timescaledb.compress, timescaledb.compress_segmentby = 'exchange, symbol, timeframe'); SELECT add_compression_policy('candles', INTERVAL '7 days'); (4) Create continuous aggregates for 5m→15m→1h→4h→1d resampling. title: Repair paper reconciliation checkpoints and atomic settlements
description: Recovery compares candle timestamps against pos.updated_time, but database save_paper_position overwrites updated_time with wall-clock time instead of the last processed candle time. This commonly empties the missed-candle range and falls back to only the last ten candles, potentially missing older downtime exits or replaying already-processed bars. Close flows also commit cash transaction, trade history, and position deletion separately, so crashes can leave inconsistent or repeatable settlement state.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Persist a distinct last-processed market-bar timestamp/ID, not a database update wall clock
- [ ] Reconcile strictly candles newer than the checkpoint in chronological order, with documented gap-fill and ambiguous-bar rules
- [ ] Make recovery idempotent when run repeatedly or after a crash at each settlement step
- [ ] Commit cash ledger entry, completed trade, and position closure atomically or via a recoverable transaction/event state machine
- [ ] Test stale checkpoints, gaps longer than ten bars, repeated reconciliation, and injected failures between settlement writes

title: Define causal paper fills and stop-gap execution math
description: Paper evaluation derives signal from the latest candle and enters at that same candle close; live partial-candle semantics are undocumented. Stop exits use low/high and fill at stop with slippage but do not account for an opening gap through the stop. Entry stop/target sizing uses the unslipped close while the actual entry is slipped. Timeout/manual/take-profit exits apply inconsistent slippage assumptions. Specify the paper execution contract and align live evaluation with recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Specify whether signals use closed candles or live partial candles and when a fill becomes executable
- [ ] Calculate stop/target distances from the actual modeled fill price
- [ ] Model adverse opening gaps through stop orders using the open when worse than the stop
- [ ] Define slippage/fees by order side and exit reason, including market timeout/manual exits versus passive targets
- [ ] Add deterministic tests for gaps, signal timing, slipped entry risk, and parity between normal evaluation and reconciliation

title: Make paper candle execution idempotent and profile-safe

If a stop closes a position but the latest signal remains active, a later poll can re-enter on that same bar and repeat fees/exits. step_all_active_profiles iterates profiles independently, while positions are keyed only by exchange/symbol; multiple active profiles for one asset can therefore manage the same position using different timeframe/strategy parameters. Define processed-bar and position/profile identity semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Store/derive a durable last-processed candle identity and prevent duplicate entry/exit side effects for repeated polls of one candle
- [ ] Define whether only closed candles or live partial candles can trigger signals/fills
- [ ] Enforce one active strategy per asset or scope positions and execution state to profile/timeframe identity
- [ ] Ensure a position closed by a bar event cannot re-open from that same event unless explicitly intended
- [ ] Add repeated-poll, stop-then-same-signal, and multiple-profile same-symbol tests

title: Paper trading accounting and execution correctness audit
description: Audit and harden the paper-trading simulator from candle/profile evaluation through simulated fills, cash and position accounting, recovery, and API reporting. Establish consistent mathematical invariants for long and short positions, prevent duplicate/conflicting executions, make recovery idempotent, and document simulation assumptions. Existing maintained paper tests currently pass but do not cover several confirmed cross-path inconsistencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Define canonical cash, reserved collateral, position value, equity, realized PnL, unrealized PnL, fees, and return-percent equations for long and short positions
- [ ] Ensure each market event/profile/account has explicit identity and cannot be processed twice or conflict silently
- [ ] Make fill, stop/target, timing, price precision, and holding-duration rules consistent across live evaluation and restart reconciliation
- [ ] Ensure persistence preserves a recoverable, auditable state across partial failures
- [ ] Validate account/profile isolation and cash-input constraints
- [ ] Add deterministic mathematical and lifecycle regression coverage; maintain efficiency under multiple profiles
notes:
Audit findings (src/paper/engine.py, ledger.py, models.py, database.py; maintained tests 21 passed): (1) Short MTM is inconsistent: PaperLedger.get_total_equity adds quantity*current_price for shorts, while engine status uses cost_basis+unrealized_pnl; short unrealized percent uses entry/current-1 rather than realized-PnL/cost-basis. This directly affects risk-based sizing. (2) Automatic/reconciled exits subtract entry+exit fees, but manual close subtracts only exit fee; trade history/PnL therefore depends on exit path. (3) Paper positions are globally unique by exchange/symbol, lack account_id/profile identity, while engine accepts account_id and profiles include timeframe/mode; same asset can be cross-owned or evaluated under competing profiles. (4) evaluate_symbol uses the latest close-derived signal and close fill, does not deduplicate candle events, uses stop levels sized before entry slippage, and does not gap-adjust stop fills; reconciliation has divergent execution math. (5) updated_time is database wall-clock on save but reconciliation treats it as market-bar checkpoint and falls back to last 10 bars; settlements span separate DB writes. (6) fixed 4-decimal price rounding and hardcoded holding_period_bars=1 can distort micro-priced assets and trade metrics. (7) deposit/withdraw do not reject negative/non-finite values; a global engine lock includes network fetch and indicator work. Existing suites pass but lack these conservation/idempotency/recovery invariants. Separate children prioritize correctness and lifecycle first, then precision/input and efficiency. Beads updates are local only; no Dolt remote is configured.
Additional ledger audit finding: short entries currently pass through record_buy and are stored as BUY with positive asset_qty, while exits are BUY_TO_COVER; add explicit SELL_SHORT/signed-quantity accounting so ledger history can independently reconcile shorts. Tracked in ema_vwap-l7v.14.

Preserve the existing single-process path and metric, pruning, in-sample labeling, and result semantics.

title: Decide Optuna process topology and data contract
description: Research and specify the supported process-parallel architecture before implementation. Compare Optuna JournalStorage for same-host processes with RDBStorage for multi-node use; do not use SQLite storage for parallel trials. Choose how candles and shared indicator frames are transferred or loaded per worker, how total trial/time budgets and per-worker sampler seeds are allocated, and which execution mode remains the default based on measured throughput.

- [ ] Document single-host process scope and explicitly defer or specify multi-node support

It states InMemoryStorage is not process-shared; JournalFileBackend locks are appropriate for same-host local filesystems but not NFS/multi-host; RDBStorage is recommended for multi-node. https://optuna.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/generated/optuna.storages.RDBStorage.html explicitly says SQLite is not recommended for parallel optimization. description: Multi-objective metric names and duplicates are not validated. Invalid or under-traded trials are completed with infinite sentinel values, remain eligible for Pareto selection, and can be emitted as Infinity in top_trials/pareto_frontier. title: Execute close-derived signals at the next tradable price
description: Strategy signals use the current candle close (including close-based crossover and pullback conditions), but BacktestEngine currently enters at that same close. title: Base Gate 3 Monte Carlo on OOS equity-relative results
description:
## Why
`StrategyValidator` currently passes the full-sample Gate 1 trade list into Monte Carlo. The simulator resamples fixed-dollar `pnl`, even though the backtest sizes positions from current equity. With fewer than two trades, it returns zero ruin probability and zero drawdown with zero simulations; the validator can accept that as a safe result. A Monte Carlo exception also leaves zero-valued risk metrics that can earn full score unless outcome handling is corrected.

## Relevant code
- `src/validator.py`: Gate 3 input selection, thresholds, exception path, metrics, and scoring.
- `src/wfo.py`: OOS window results and combined OOS trade data. This task depends on child `ema_vwap-4rn.3` exposing a stable chronological OOS result stream.
- `src/monte_carlo.py`: input representation, sampling, equity path, drawdown/ruin calculation, RNG, and result fields.
- `src/backtester.py` / `src/risk_manager.py`: realized trade PnL, fees, and equity-based position sizing.
- `tests/test_monte_carlo.py` and `tests/test_validator.py`.

## Required work
1. Use only OOS trade/return evidence from the completed WFO windows for Gate 3. Preserve chronological ordering and exclude warm-up and IS observations.
2. Simulate returns relative to account equity (or an equivalent well-defined R-multiple plus position-risk sizing) and reapply returns to evolving simulated equity. Do not treat fixed-dollar historical PnLs or `Trade.pnl_pct` (which is relative to position value) as account returns without conversion.
3. Define the risk event precisely. The current rule combines a 50% peak-to-trough drawdown with ending equity at or below 50% of initial capital; document whether both conditions represent the same event or should be separate metrics. Align result/UI wording with the chosen definition.
4. Make insufficient OOS trade count, invalid outcomes, and simulation exceptions explicit unavailable/non-passing states. Never default unavailable risk to 0% or award full score. Validate finite inputs and positive initial capital.
5. Use a local seeded random generator rather than mutating NumPy global RNG state. Preserve reproducibility for a configured seed.
6. Profile the simulation at realistic trade/simulation sizes; if the nested loop is material, use bounded batches/vectorization and record a before/after benchmark without allocating an unbounded simulation-by-trade matrix.

## Tests
Add controlled outcomes that verify OOS-only sample selection, chronological returns, equity scaling, fee inclusion, the exact drawdown/ruin event, insufficient sample and invalid-input behavior, deterministic seeding, and no global RNG side effect. Add a validator test proving missing/failed Monte Carlo evidence cannot pass or receive full points. Add a repeatable benchmark or documented profiling result if implementation changes the sampling algorithm.
design: Consume a WFO-produced chronological OOS trade or per-period return stream, not Gate 1 trades. Prefer storing account-equity-relative realized return at the point of each trade (or enough risk/equity metadata to derive it) and compound it over each simulated path. Keep the simulation core independent of presentation. Return an explicit simulation status and sample size. Use `numpy.random.Generator`; batch large work if measurement justifies it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Gate 3 receives OOS-only evidence from WFO, with warm-up/IS trades excluded and OOS chronology preserved.
- [ ] Simulated outcomes scale with evolving account equity consistently with the documented position-sizing model and include net costs.
- [ ] Ruin/drawdown event definitions and user-visible metric names are unambiguous and tested.
- [ ] Insufficient trades, invalid data, or simulation errors are explicitly unavailable/non-passing and cannot appear as zero risk or earn full score.
- [ ] Seeded runs are reproducible without changing global NumPy RNG state.
- [ ] Tests cover provenance, sizing, risk event, low sample, invalid input, deterministic behavior, and validator score/status handling.
- [ ] Simulation performance is profiled; any vectorization is bounded in memory and supported by a reproducible benchmark.
notes: Parent epic: `ema_vwap-4rn`. Depends on WFO child `ema_vwap-4rn.3` for trustworthy OOS data. Coordinate final threshold and unavailable-result semantics with child `ema_vwap-4rn.1`.

title: Correct Gate 2 WFE and OOS return definitions
description:
## Why
The Gate 2 UI describes walk-forward efficiency as OOS Sharpe / IS Sharpe, but `WalkForwardEngine.run()` calculates the ratio of mean total-return percentages. Its branches assign 100% when average IS return is negative and OOS is nonnegative, and 0% for other nonpositive-IS cases. The validator labels `avg_out_of_sample_return_pct` as `oos_total_return_pct` and applies the minimum OOS return threshold to that average. These values do not implement the documented meaning and can mischaracterize performance across unequal window lengths.

## Relevant code
- `src/wfo.py`: window backtests, `is_sharpe`/`oos_sharpe`, `is_returns`/`oos_returns`, WFE calculation, window output, and aggregate return fields.
- `src/validator.py`: Gate 2 metric extraction and threshold checks.
- `src/web/index.html`: WFE help text and threshold labels.
- `tests/test_wfo.py`, `tests/test_validator.py`, and API/UI tests as appropriate.

## Required work
1. Implement WFE according to the public contract: use comparable annualized IS/OOS Sharpe measurements, explicitly define how per-window values are aggregated, and remove arbitrary 100%/0% substitutions for negative or near-zero IS performance. Undefined or insufficient evidence must be represented explicitly and cannot pass the WFE threshold silently.
2. Report average OOS window return under an accurate name. Separately calculate and expose a sequential aggregate OOS return across the contiguous, non-overlapping OOS windows; use the documented aggregate for `min_oos_return_pct`.
3. Preserve window-level IS/OOS returns and Sharpe values so users can audit the aggregate and tests can verify its construction. Keep names/types consistent between `WalkForwardEngine`, `StrategyValidator`, serialized reports, and the UI.
4. Confirm OOS windows remain contiguous and non-overlapping and that warm-up history is not counted as OOS performance.

## Tests
Add deterministic tests using controlled window results for positive, negative, zero, and near-zero IS Sharpe; different IS/OOS durations; unequal window returns; and no valid windows. Assert the exact WFE aggregation and aggregate return formula, the metric names in the validation report, and the Gate 2 pass/caution/fail behavior at threshold boundaries.
design: Honor the existing UI contract of OOS Sharpe divided by IS Sharpe. Use paired per-window annualized Sharpe values and select/document a robust aggregation across windows (median is a candidate); require a meaningful positive IS denominator or mark the ratio unavailable, rather than fabricating 100% or 0%. Because OOS windows are contiguous and non-overlapping, compute the sequential aggregate return from their return factors, and retain mean window return as a separate diagnostic. Coordinate metric names with Gate 3 so the OOS trade/return stream can be reused.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] WFE is calculated from the documented annualized Sharpe quantities, with its window aggregation method stated in code/API/UI documentation and tested.
- [ ] Zero, negative, and near-zero IS Sharpe have explicit non-arbitrary handling and cannot turn poor or undefined evidence into 100% WFE.
- [ ] Average per-window OOS return and sequential aggregate OOS return are distinct, accurately named metrics.
- [ ] `min_oos_return_pct` checks the chosen aggregate OOS return, not an unlabeled average.
- [ ] Window-level values remain auditable; warm-up bars are excluded from OOS results.
- [ ] Deterministic tests cover formula cases, unequal window lengths/returns, edge cases, and threshold decisions.
notes: Parent epic: `ema_vwap-4rn`. This task should produce the OOS trades or return series needed by child `ema_vwap-4rn.4` (Monte Carlo); expose them in a stable internal report/result field and avoid sending an unnecessarily large trade list to browser clients.

title: Correct Gate 1 equity drawdown and final-exit costs
description:
## Why
Gate 1 uses `BacktestEngine` equity analytics. The equity curve records the first candle only after any entry fee and mark-to-market, so max drawdown can omit loss from initial capital to that first recorded value. Also, normal stock exits charge SEC and FINRA fees, while the end-of-data close path appears to charge only taker fee. Both can understate the risk or overstate performance used by Gate 1 and later Monte Carlo.

## Relevant code
- `src/backtester.py`: equity curve recording, max drawdown calculation, normal exit fee calculation, and final end-of-data liquidation.
- `src/validator.py`: Gate 1 consumes total return, Sharpe, and max drawdown.
- `tests/test_backtester.py` and `tests/test_validator.py`.

## Required work
1. Include initial account equity as the opening peak for drawdown calculations, while preserving a coherent timestamp/equity-curve contract for API and chart consumers.
2. Apply the same applicable stock regulatory fees to end-of-data exits as to normal exits; avoid charging the entry fee twice and keep recorded trade fees/PnL consistent.
3. Verify the equity curve, final equity, net profit, return, max drawdown, and trade PnL reconcile for a first-bar loss and for a stock position liquidated at the final bar.

## Tests
Add deterministic backtester tests where a fee or first-bar adverse move makes drawdown exceed the value computed from the first post-entry point, and where end-of-data stock liquidation includes SEC/FINRA fees. Assert reconciliation among trade-level PnL/fees, final equity, total return, and drawdown.
design: Preserve existing backtest API outputs unless an equity curve contract change is necessary; if the opening-capital point is added, verify chart consumers tolerate it. Reuse a shared exit-fee calculation so normal and end-of-data liquidation cannot drift. Include all costs in realized PnL and in equity before calculating performance statistics.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Max drawdown is measured from at least initial capital and includes initial execution costs and losses.
- [ ] End-of-data stock liquidation applies the same applicable regulatory fee rules as a normal exit.
- [ ] Final equity, net profit, total return, equity curve, trade PnL, and fee totals reconcile without double charging.
- [ ] Focused deterministic tests cover first-recorded-point drawdown and stock end-of-data fees; existing backtester and validator tests pass.
notes: Parent epic: `ema_vwap-4rn`. This task corrects Gate 1 inputs consumed by all downstream validation, not just the displayed Gate 1 metrics.

title: Wire validation thresholds and align gate outcomes
description:
## Why
The Validation Gates settings are saved and displayed, but `validateStrategyConfig()` does not include `criteria` in its POST body. `validate_strategy_endpoint()` therefore constructs default `ValidationCriteria` for normal UI requests. Separately, a gate can have `status=CAUTION` and `passed=True`, so the `gates_passed` count can describe a caution result as a pass. A Gate 3 exception leaves risk metrics at zero, allowing the score calculation to award full risk points.

## Relevant code
- `src/web/app.js`: `validateStrategyConfig()`, existing settings load/save, and settings control IDs.
- `src/app.py`: `ValidateStrategyRequest` and `/api/strategy/validate`.
- `src/validator.py`: `ValidationCriteria`, status transitions, pass count, overall status, and score synthesis.
- Existing tests: `tests/test_validator.py` and API/frontend tests as appropriate.

## Required work
1. Pass the currently configured threshold values using the `ValidationCriteria` field names when the UI starts validation. Preserve API default behavior when an external caller omits `criteria`.
2. Verify values persist/load consistently and resolve duplicate DOM IDs or stale cross-wired fields that cause a threshold to read from the wrong control.
3. Define and enforce one contract for PASS, CAUTION, FAIL, unavailable, `passed`, `gates_passed`, overall status, and score. A caution must not be counted as an unqualified pass; unavailable/exception metrics must not be interpreted as zero risk or earn full Gate 3 points.
4. Validate threshold input ranges at the API/configuration boundary where appropriate, with messages identifying the invalid field.

## Tests
Add focused API or unit tests proving that non-default submitted criteria affect their corresponding gate decisions, omitted criteria use defaults, threshold values survive settings load/save and request construction, invalid criteria are rejected, and PASS/CAUTION/FAIL/unavailable reports have coherent counts and scores.
design: Use the existing `ValidationCriteria` dataclass field names as the request contract. Keep API defaults for older clients. Prefer `gates_passed` to count only gates whose final status is PASS; represent CAUTION and unavailable results distinctly and ensure overall status derives from the individual outcomes. Scores may remain partial for measured caution results, but missing or failed measurements must not receive full credit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] UI-triggered validation sends all supported ValidationCriteria values and the server applies them to the run.
- [ ] Requests without criteria remain backward-compatible and use documented defaults.
- [ ] Duplicate or cross-wired settings controls do not cause one field to overwrite another.
- [ ] `passed`, gate status, `gates_passed`, overall status, and score follow a documented consistent policy.
- [ ] Gate exceptions and unavailable metrics cannot be treated as zero risk or receive full risk points.
- [ ] Focused tests cover criteria propagation, defaults, validation errors, and outcome semantics.
notes: Related prior work: closed `ema_vwap-tei` added threshold controls and API criteria support, but the current frontend validation request still omits the criteria payload. Parent epic: `ema_vwap-4rn`.

title: Harden the three-gate strategy validation system
description:
## Why
A review of `src/validator.py`, `src/wfo.py`, `src/monte_carlo.py`, and `src/backtester.py` found that several gate labels do not match their implemented metrics, risk simulation is based on in-sample fixed-dollar PnL, and validation requests do not use the configured UI thresholds. The existing validation tests pass but do not pin the mathematical definitions or these failure cases.

## Current findings
- The UI validation request omits `criteria`; the API constructs default `ValidationCriteria`, so edits in the Validation Gates settings do not control validation. The closed threshold-exposure issue `ema_vwap-tei` did not resolve this runtime request wiring.
- Gate 1 drawdown starts from the first recorded equity point rather than explicitly including starting capital. Stock end-of-data liquidation applies taker fees but appears to omit the regulatory fees charged on normal exits.
- Gate 2 documents WFE as OOS Sharpe divided by IS Sharpe but calculates a ratio of average total-return percentages. It assigns arbitrary values for nonpositive IS returns. The field `avg_out_of_sample_return_pct` is consumed as `oos_total_return_pct`, and the minimum OOS return gate therefore checks an average window return rather than a clearly defined aggregate.
- Gate 3 simulates the full-sample Gate 1 trade list as fixed-dollar PnL, reports zero risk when fewer than two trades prevent simulation, and can award full risk points when simulation errors occur.
- Several CAUTION outcomes leave `passed=True`; gate counts and scores can therefore disagree with the displayed gate status.

## Scope
Correct and test the configured-threshold path, outcome semantics, Gate 1 account-risk calculations, Gate 2 metric definitions and OOS aggregation, and Gate 3 OOS risk simulation. Add focused tests that establish the chosen behavior, including degenerate and failed-simulation cases. Preserve current API compatibility where practical and document intentional behavior changes.

## Out of scope
Do not retune default financial thresholds or claim that passing these historical tests guarantees live profitability. Do not redesign the strategy, optimizer, deployment process, or portfolio risk engine as part of this work.
design: Use the current UI/API contract as the starting point and make each metric definition explicit. For WFE, follow the documented OOS Sharpe / IS Sharpe meaning unless a product decision intentionally changes the contract; define aggregation across windows and guard zero or negative denominators without assigning arbitrary 100% efficiency. Report average per-window OOS return separately from compounded/aggregate OOS return. Preserve per-trade OOS account-relative returns (or an equivalent return-on-equity/R-multiple measure) so Monte Carlo can rescale outcomes as simulated equity changes. A CAUTION or unavailable result must not count as an unqualified PASS; missing/failed risk calculations must not be scored as zero risk.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every exposed Validation Gates threshold used by the UI is sent to the validation API and applied to that run; API callers that omit criteria retain documented defaults.
- [ ] Gate status, `passed`, `gates_passed`, overall status, and score agree for PASS, CAUTION, FAIL, and unavailable/error outcomes; unavailable metrics never receive full risk points.
- [ ] Gate 1 drawdown includes starting equity and all applicable fees, including stock regulatory fees on end-of-data exits.
- [ ] Gate 2 WFE definition matches its public help text, has explicit behavior for zero/negative IS performance, and does not silently substitute average window return for aggregate OOS return.
- [ ] Gate 3 uses OOS evidence, models equity-relative trade outcomes consistently with position sizing, and reports insufficient evidence as unavailable/non-passing rather than zero risk.
- [ ] Focused deterministic tests cover formulas, thresholds, gate status/count/score consistency, low-sample and error cases, stock final-exit costs, and OOS trade provenance.
- [ ] Existing validator, WFO, Monte Carlo, and backtester tests pass; API/UI behavior and metric names are documented where changed.
notes: Implementation is decomposed into children: (1) criteria wiring and report semantics, (2) Gate 1 accounting, (3) Gate 2 WFE/OOS definitions, (4) Gate 3 OOS-based Monte Carlo. Gate 3 depends on Gate 2 exposing the OOS trade stream or equivalent OOS return series. Relevant baseline: `pytest tests/test_validator.py tests/test_wfo.py tests/test_monte_carlo.py -q` currently passes 24 tests, but those tests do not establish these contracts.

title: Increase default Strategy Validation trial budget and tune per-window Optuna bounds
description: Default validation budget is n_trials = 30 in both API (src/routes/backtest_opt.py:L579) and UI (src/web/app.js:L2567). Across 5 windows, compute_wfo_auto_params clamps trials per window to 25. For an 8-dimensional strategy hyperparameter space, Optuna TPESampler requires 10-15 random startup trials alone. With only 25 trials, parameter search is largely random exploration, causing in-sample optimization to select noisy parameters that fail out-of-sample and artificially fail Gate 2. Plan: 1. In src/routes/backtest_opt.py (ValidateStrategyRequest), increase default n_trials to 250 (allowing >=50 trials per window). 2. In src/web/app.js (validateStrategyConfig / UI defaults), increase default validation trials to 250. 3. In src/wfo.py (compute_wfo_auto_params), adjust formula clamp from max(25, min(n_trials, raw_trials)) to min(n_trials, max(50, raw_trials)) to ensure at least 50 trials per window when budget permits. 4. Add UI presets/toggle for validation rigor (e.g. Fast: 150 trials vs Thorough: 300-500 trials). 5. Update and verify tests in tests/test_validator.py and tests/test_wfo.py.

title: Time-normalize Walk-Forward Efficiency (WFE) ratio and fix Gate 2 OOS return metrics
description: 1. In src/wfo.py, WFE is computed as (avg_oos_ret / avg_is_ret) * 100. Because in_sample_ratio = 0.7, In-Sample data is 2.33x longer in calendar duration than Out-of-Sample. Comparing unannualized percentage return directly depresses WFE by 2.33x, causing strategies with identical daily return in OOS as in IS to receive only 42.8% WFE and fail Gate 2 (min 50%). 2. In src/validator.py, avg_out_of_sample_return_pct is stored under the dictionary key oos_total_return_pct, confusing average window return with compounded cumulative return. 3. In src/validator.py, _g1_metric_scores uses raw Sharpe for drawdown_penalized_sharpe and is missing drawdown_penalized_sortino. Plan: 1. In src/wfo.py, time-normalize WFE using candle count ratio: (avg_oos_ret / oos_bars) / (avg_is_ret / is_bars) * 100, or compute annualized return ratio / OOS Sharpe / IS Sharpe. 2. In src/validator.py, clarify Gate 2 metrics to report both avg_oos_window_return_pct and oos_cumulative_return_pct. 3. Fix _g1_metric_scores to evaluate drawdown_penalized_sharpe and drawdown_penalized_sortino with proper backtest result attributes. 4. Update tests in tests/test_validator.py and tests/test_wfo.py.
close_reason: Completed: Time-normalized WFE by candle count ratio, differentiated avg and cumulative OOS return metrics in Gate 2, and fixed Gate 1 drawdown-penalized metric scores.

title: Implement timeframe-aware bars_per_day scaling for Walk-Forward Optimization (WFO)
description: compute_wfo_auto_params and WalkForwardEngine.__init__ in src/wfo.py default to bars_per_day = 288.0 (only valid for 5m crypto). StrategyValidator.validate in src/validator.py calls WalkForwardEngine without passing bars_per_day or timeframe. This distorts OOS window calculations: 15m (96 bars/day) results in 45-day OOS windows instead of 15-day windows; 1h (24 bars/day) results in 180-day (6-month) OOS windows and collapses window count to 3; 4h (6 bars/day) exceeds total candle count and forces negative window count calculation. Plan: 1. Update StrategyValidator.validate to compute bars_per_day from df_candles timestamp delta or lookup get_timeframe_spec(timeframe).bars_per_day_crypto and pass to WalkForwardEngine. 2. Update WalkForwardEngine to dynamically derive bars_per_day when not explicitly passed. 3. Adjust target_oos_days scaling by timeframe (e.g. 14 days for <=5m, 21-30 days for 15m-30m, 45-60 days for 1h-4h). 4. Add unit tests for window/step calculation across 5m, 15m, 1h, and 4h in tests/test_wfo.py.
close_reason: Implemented timeframe-aware bars_per_day and target_oos_days scaling in WFO and StrategyValidator. **Impact:** Reduces API calls and DB round-trips by 50-80% for multi-timeframe sweeps; ~1-5s saved per symbol
**Effort:** medium
**Files:** src/batch_optimizer.py

title: OPTIMIZATION: Cache strategy and risk manager instances in PaperTradingEngine
description:
PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: PaperTradingEngine.evaluate_symbol in src/paper/engine.py (line 194) creates new RiskManager and EmaVwapStrategy instances per call. In step_all_active_profiles, this happens for every active profile every poll cycle (default 15s). These objects are stateless and only depend on params which are cached in the registry.

**Current Code:** New RiskManager(params) and EmaVwapStrategy(params) created per call.

**Fix:** Cache strategy and risk manager instances keyed by params hash (or profile ID) in PaperTradingEngine. Reuse when params haven't changed. Add a _strategy_cache and _risk_manager_cache dict.

**Impact:** Eliminates object allocation and indicator recomputation per poll cycle; ~5-10ms saved per profile per poll
**Effort:** low
**Files:** src/paper/engine.py

title: OPTIMIZATION: Vectorize BacktestEngine.run to replace Python loop with NumPy operations
description:
PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: BacktestEngine.run in src/backtester.py (line 234) uses Python loop over bars instead of vectorized operations. With 1000-5000 bars and 100+ trials, this is the hottest path.

**Current Code:** Main backtest loop iterates bar-by-bar in pure Python. NumPy arrays pre-extracted but loop body has complex branching, dict lookups, and method calls.

**Fix:** Vectorize using NumPy/pandas operations where possible: pre-compute entry/exit signals as boolean masks, use cumulative operations for equity curve. For stop/trailing logic which is path-dependent, consider Numba JIT (@numba.jit) on the inner loop or rewrite in Cython. At minimum, move fee/position sizing calculations out of the loop.

**Impact:** 10-50x speedup on backtest execution; critical for Optuna (100 trials x 1000 bars = 100k iterations)
**Effort:** high
**Files:** src/backtester.py

title: OPTIMIZATION: Precompute shared indicators in OptunaOptimizer to avoid recomputation per trial
description:
PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: EmaVwapStrategy.generate_signals in src/strategy.py recomputes shared indicators (VWAP, VWAP slope, ATR, volume SMA) for every Optuna trial. These shared indicators only depend on base params (fast_ema, slow_ema, trend_ema, atr_period, etc.) and not on trial-specific params.

**Current Code:** Strategy generates signals by computing EMA/VWAP/ATR fresh for every trial. Shared indicators recomputed identically across all trials in a study.

**Fix:** Add precomputed_indicators support to OptunaOptimizer.optimize - compute shared indicators once per study using compute_shared_indicators, pass to each trial's objective function. OptunaOptimizer already accepts precomputed_indicators in BacktestEngine but doesn't use it.

**Impact:** Reduces per-trial indicator computation by ~60-80%; with 100 trials, saves ~500ms-2s per optimization run
**Effort:** medium
**Files:** src/strategy.py, src/optimizer.py

title: OPTIMIZATION: Add caching to DataLoader.load_candles for donor timeframe fetches
description:
PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: DataLoader.load_candles in src/data_loader.py (line 348) recursively calls itself for donor timeframe without caching the donor result. When multiple higher timeframes need the same donor (e.g., 3m, 15m, 30m all from 1m), the donor fetch is repeated.

**Current Code:** Recursive call to load_candles for donor TF without caching donor result at call site.

**Fix:** Add a local LRU cache on load_candles for (exchange, symbol, timeframe, limit, days) or use functools.lru_cache on a private _load_candles_raw method. Return cached donor DataFrame to avoid re-fetching.

**Impact:** Avoids redundant API calls and DB reads when multiple timeframes share a donor; ~100-500ms per donor fetch saved
**Effort:** low
**Files:** src/data_loader.py

title: OPTIMIZATION: Add memoization to compute_slope_bounds_from_df
description:
PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION: compute_slope_bounds_from_df in src/indicators.py (line 78) recalculates VWAP slope bounds for same symbol/timeframe across batch optimization runs. The function performs expensive percentile calculations on VWAP slopes.

**Current Code:** Function called during every batch optimization run for same symbol/timeframe but results not cached.

**Fix:** Add functools.lru_cache decorator with hashable key (timeframe + hash of slope values) or use module-level cache dict keyed by (exchange, symbol, timeframe). Cache static fallback bounds per timeframe and live-calibrated bounds per symbol+timeframe combination.

**Impact:** Eliminates redundant VWAP slope percentile calculations across batch runs; ~10-50ms saved per combo
**Effort:** low
**Files:** src/indicators.py

title: SECURITY: Encrypt secrets at rest (not just mask for display)
description:
MEDIUM SECURITY ISSUE: SettingsManager in src/settings.py (line 30) masks secrets for display (last 4 chars) but stores them in plaintext in SQLite database. No encryption at rest.

**Attack Vector:** Database file theft, backup exposure, SQL injection reading settings table.

**Impact:** Full credential compromise for all configured exchanges and providers.

**Remediation:**
1. Encrypt secrets at rest using Fernet/AES-GCM with key from environment/key management
2. Use envelope encryption
4. Rotate keys periodically

**Files to modify:**
- src/settings.py: Add encryption/decryption
- src/database.py: Store encrypted values

title: SECURITY: Add missing security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
description:
MEDIUM SECURITY ISSUE: FastAPI application in src/app.py doesn't set security headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.

**Attack Vector:** Clickjacking, MIME sniffing, CSP bypass, mixed content, iframe embedding.

**Impact:** Client-side attack surface expansion, reduced defense-in-depth.

**Remediation:**
1. Add middleware to set security headers
2. Use fastapi.middleware.trustedhost.TrustedHostMiddleware
3. Implement CSP appropriate for Plotly/JS requirements

**Files to modify:**
- src/app.py: Add security headers middleware

title: SECURITY: Secure default settings - bind to localhost, disable reload
description:
MEDIUM SECURITY ISSUE: Application binds to 0.0.0.0:8080 by default with reload enabled via RELOAD env var in src/app.py (line 2746). No production deployment hardening.

**Attack Vector:** Network exposure on all interfaces, auto-reload in production enables code injection via file write.

**Impact:** Unauthorized network access, potential RCE if reload enabled and file write accessible.

**Remediation:**
1. Default to 127.0.0.1
2. Require explicit HOST=0.0.0.0 for external access
3. Disable reload in production
4. Use reverse proxy with TLS

**Files to modify:**
- src/app.py: Change default HOST to 127.0.0.1, require explicit override

title: SECURITY: Fix information disclosure in error messages
description:
MEDIUM SECURITY ISSUE: Exception details logged and potentially returned to clients in HTTP 500 responses in src/app.py (line 264). Stack traces may reveal internal architecture, database paths, and implementation details.

**Attack Vector:** Triggering errors via malformed requests to gather system intelligence.

**Impact:** Information leakage aiding further attacks, path disclosure, technology stack enumeration.

**Remediation:**
1. Use generic error messages for client responses
2. Log full details server-side only
3. Implement structured error handling with safe client-facing messages

**Files to modify:**
- src/app.py: Standardize error handling to not leak details

title: Paper profile primary key prevents cross-timeframe parameter reuse

Paper profiles use composite primary key (exchange, symbol, timeframe, strategy_mode) in DB. This means parameters optimized for 5m cannot be reused for 15m/1h without re-optimizing, even though the same strategy parameters might work across timeframes.

When deploying from Optuna (5m) to paper trading, if the paper trader later runs on 15m, it won't find the profile because timeframe differs.

# Batch Sweep: All Multi-Objective Metric Combinations (single-timeframe gate)

## Description

Add an `★ All Combinations` option to the **Multi-Metric Objective Set** dropdown
(`#batch-multi-metric-select`) in the Batch Sweep UI. When selected and exactly **one
timeframe** is checked, the sweep expands into one sequential sub-run per valid 2-metric
Pareto combination from the allowed multi-objective pool. The gate contract (single
timeframe) is identical to the single-objective All Metrics bead.

This is the multi-objective counterpart to the single-objective "All Metrics" bead.
Implement after (or in parallel with) the single-objective bead.

## Canonical Multi-Objective Metric Pool

Sourced from `src/optimizer.py` validation logic:
`allowed_metrics = TARGET_METRICS | {"max_drawdown_pct"}`

Full pool (11 metrics):
- `sharpe_ratio`, `drawdown_penalized_sharpe`, `calmar_ratio`, `sortino_ratio`,
  `drawdown_penalized_sortino`, `ulcer_index`, `profit_factor`, `net_profit`,
  `total_return_pct`, `win_rate`, `max_drawdown_pct`

**Practical curated set for "All Combinations"** — rather than C(11,2) = 55 pairs (which
would be prohibitively slow), use a curated list of **high-value pairs** that are
meaningfully non-redundant. Recommended default set (12 pairs):

| Pair | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `sharpe_ratio\|max_drawdown_pct` | Risk-adjusted return vs. tail risk |
| `sharpe_ratio\|total_return_pct` | Risk-adjusted vs. raw return |
| `sharpe_ratio\|win_rate` | Consistency vs. efficiency |
| `sortino_ratio\|max_drawdown_pct` | Downside-risk adjusted vs. tail |
| `calmar_ratio\|max_drawdown_pct` | Return/DD ratio vs. DD magnitude |
| `drawdown_penalized_sharpe\|max_drawdown_pct` | DD-robust Sharpe vs. DD |
| `drawdown_penalized_sortino\|max_drawdown_pct` | DD-robust Sortino vs. DD |
| `profit_factor\|total_return_pct` | Edge quality vs. total return |
| `profit_factor\|max_drawdown_pct` | Edge quality vs. risk |
| `net_profit\|max_drawdown_pct` | Absolute profit vs. risk |
| `total_return_pct\|win_rate` | Return vs. consistency |
| `ulcer_index\|total_return_pct` | Recovery stress vs. return |

> **Design decision required**: Should the set be fixed (hardcoded) or user-configurable
> (e.g., a checklist of pairs)? This bead assumes the fixed curated 12-pair default.
> A follow-up bead can add a custom pair builder.

## Backend Changes

### `src/app.py` — `start_batch_optimize`
```python
ALL_MULTI_PAIRS = [
    ["sharpe_ratio", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["sharpe_ratio", "total_return_pct"],
    ["sharpe_ratio", "win_rate"],
    ["sortino_ratio", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["calmar_ratio", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["drawdown_penalized_sharpe", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["drawdown_penalized_sortino", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["profit_factor", "total_return_pct"],
    ["profit_factor", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["net_profit", "max_drawdown_pct"],
    ["total_return_pct", "win_rate"],
    ["ulcer_index", "total_return_pct"],
]

MULTI_ALL_SENTINEL = "all_combinations"

if req.enable_multi_objective and req.multi_objective_metrics == [MULTI_ALL_SENTINEL]:
    if len(req.timeframes) != 1:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="'All Combinations' multi-objective requires exactly one timeframe."
        )
    configs = [
        BatchOptimizerConfig(
            ...shared fields from req...,
            enable_multi_objective=True,
            multi_objective_metrics=pair,
            target_metric=pair[0],        # reference metric for leaderboard storage key
        )
        for pair in ALL_MULTI_PAIRS
    ]
    background_tasks.add_task(_run_all_metrics_batch_task, configs)
    return {"status": "started", "message": f"All multi-objective combinations started ({len(configs)} pairs)."}
```

The `_run_all_metrics_batch_task` function (defined in the single-objective bead) is reused
without modification — it is metric-agnostic and works for both single and multi-objective
configs.

### Progress label in current_combo
For multi-objective runs, format as:
`[sharpe_ratio|max_drawdown_pct — 1/12]`

## Frontend Changes

### `src/web/index.html` — `#batch-multi-metric-select`
Add as **first** `<option>`:
```html
<option value="all_combinations">★ All Combinations (Single Timeframe Only)</option>
```
Add hint element below the select:
```html
<small id="batch-all-multi-hint" style="display:none; color: var(--accent-amber);">
  ★ Runs 12 curated Pareto-pairs. Select exactly one timeframe.
</small>
```

### `src/web/app.js` — `syncBatchMetricUI()` (extend from single-objective bead)
Add multi-objective sentinel check:
```js
const multiVal = document.getElementById("batch-multi-metric-select")?.value;
if (isMultiMode && multiVal === "all_combinations") {
  // same TF-count gate logic as single-objective all_metrics
}
```

### `startBatchSweep()` — payload serialization
When `objectiveMode === "multi"` and `multiMetricValue === "all_combinations"`:
```js
body: JSON.stringify({
  ...
  enable_multi_objective: true,
  multi_objective_metrics: ["all_combinations"],  // sentinel
  target_metric: "all_combinations",              // backend checks this
})
```

The backend intercepts `multi_objective_metrics == ["all_combinations"]` before validation
so the normal `OptunaOptimizer` metric validation is never reached.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `#batch-multi-metric-select` has `★ All Combinations` as first option
- [ ] Hint element appears when `all_combinations` is selected
- [ ] Run button disabled (red hint) when `all_combinations` + multiple timeframes
- [ ] Run button enabled (amber hint) when `all_combinations` + exactly one timeframe
- [ ] Backend receives sentinel `multi_objective_metrics: ["all_combinations"]` and expands to 12 pairs
- [ ] Backend returns HTTP 400 if sentinel + `len(timeframes) != 1`
- [ ] Each pair sub-run saves its own leaderboard row with `target_metric` = `"pair[0]|pair[1]"` format
- [ ] Progress label shows `[metric1|metric2 — N/12]`
- [ ] `_run_all_metrics_batch_task` is reused without forking (no duplication)
- [ ] All 451 existing tests pass; add ≥1 unit test for the `all_combinations` expansion

# Batch Sweep: All Metrics — Single Objective (single-timeframe gate)

## Description

Add an `★ All Metrics` option to the **Batch Rank Metric** dropdown (`#batch-metric-select`)
in the Batch Sweep UI. When selected and exactly **one timeframe** is checked, the sweep
expands internally into one sequential sub-run per metric (10 total: all entries in
`optimizer.TARGET_METRICS` excluding the `"sharpe"` alias), producing one leaderboard row
per `symbol × metric` pair. The option is **disabled in the UI** (button locked, warning
shown) whenever more than one timeframe checkbox is active, and the backend enforces this
with HTTP 400.

## Canonical Single-Objective Metric Set

Sourced from `src/optimizer.py::TARGET_METRICS` (excluding the `"sharpe"` alias):

| Key | Direction |
|---|---|
| `sharpe_ratio` | maximize |
| `drawdown_penalized_sharpe` | maximize |
| `calmar_ratio` | maximize |
| `sortino_ratio` | maximize |
| `drawdown_penalized_sortino` | maximize |
| `ulcer_index` | **minimize** |
| `profit_factor` | maximize |
| `net_profit` | maximize |
| `total_return_pct` | maximize |
| `win_rate` | maximize |

## Backend Changes

### `src/app.py` — `BatchOptimizeRequest`
No structural change needed. `target_metric: str = "sharpe_ratio"` already accepts
arbitrary strings. The sentinel value `"all_metrics"` is intercepted before
`BatchOptimizerConfig` is constructed.

### `src/app.py` — `start_batch_optimize`
```python
ALL_SINGLE_METRICS = [
    "sharpe_ratio", "drawdown_penalized_sharpe", "calmar_ratio",
    "sortino_ratio", "drawdown_penalized_sortino", "ulcer_index",
    "profit_factor", "net_profit", "total_return_pct", "win_rate",
]

if req.target_metric == "all_metrics":
    if len(req.timeframes) != 1:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="'all_metrics' requires exactly one timeframe to be selected."
        )
    configs = [
        BatchOptimizerConfig(
            ...shared fields from req...,
            timeframes=req.timeframes,   # single-element list
            target_metric=metric,
            enable_multi_objective=False,
        )
        for metric in ALL_SINGLE_METRICS
    ]
    background_tasks.add_task(_run_all_metrics_batch_task, configs)
    return {"status": "started", "message": f"All-metrics sweep started ({len(configs)} metrics)."}
```

### `src/app.py` — `_run_all_metrics_batch_task`
New background task function (not modifying `_run_batch_task`):
```python
def _run_all_metrics_batch_task(configs: list[BatchOptimizerConfig]) -> None:
    from src.batch_optimizer import _update_state
    for i, cfg in enumerate(configs):
        if get_batch_state().get("cancelled"):
            _update_state(running=False, error="Batch sweep cancelled")
            return
        # Patch current_combo to include metric context
        _update_state(current_combo=f"[{cfg.target_metric} — {i+1}/{len(configs)}]")
        try:
            BatchOptimizer(cfg).run()
        except Exception as exc:
            _update_state(running=False, error=str(exc))
            return
    _update_state(running=False, done=_batch_state.get("total", 0))
```

### Progress Accounting
`_update_state(total=len(symbols) * len(ALL_SINGLE_METRICS))` — each `symbol × metric`
counts as one combo for progress. Timeframe is fixed (single), so it does not multiply.
The per-metric `BatchOptimizer.run()` must call `_update_state(done=...)` incrementally.
Review whether `BatchOptimizer.run()` increments `done` itself or if the wrapper must.
Adjust as needed to avoid double-counting.

## Frontend Changes

### `src/web/index.html` — `#batch-metric-select`
Add as **first** `<option>`:
```html
<option value="all_metrics">★ All Metrics (Single Timeframe Only)</option>
```
Add a hint `<small>` element directly below the `<select>`:
```html
<small id="batch-all-metrics-hint" style="display:none; color: var(--accent-amber);">
  ⚠ All Metrics mode runs one sweep per metric. Select exactly one timeframe.
</small>
```

title: SECURITY: Use full UUID4 for trade IDs instead of 8-char truncation
description:
LOW SECURITY ISSUE: Trade IDs in src/paper/engine.py (line 348) generated using uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] - only 32 bits of entropy. Predictable and collision-prone under high volume.

**Attack Vector:** Trade ID prediction, collision attacks on audit trail integrity.

**Impact:** Audit log integrity compromise, potential trade record manipulation.

**Remediation:**
1. Use full UUID4 (128 bits) or cryptographically secure random bytes
2. Consider ULID for ordering + entropy

**Files to modify:**
- src/paper/engine.py: Use full UUID4 for trade IDs

title: deployOptunaToPaper validation_report not persisted to paper_profiles

deployOptunaToPaper() includes validation_report in the deploy payload, but the DeployPaperProfileRequest model and save_paper_profile() don't have a validation_report_json field. The paper_profiles table has validation_report_json column but it's never populated.

Fix: Add validation_report_json to DeployPaperProfileRequest, pass it to save_paper_profile(), and store it in the DB.

title: deployCurrentBacktestToPaper uses total_return_pct as optuna_score proxy
description:
deployCurrentBacktestToPaper() uses the backtest's total_return_pct as the optuna_score when deploying to paper profile. This is misleading because:
- total_return_pct is not the optimization metric (could be sharpe, calmar, etc.)
- It's not comparable to actual Optuna scores
- The paper profile's optuna_score field becomes meaningless for backtest-deployed profiles

Fix: Pass the actual target metric value from the backtest results (e.g., sharpe_ratio if that was the objective) instead of total_return_pct.
